Export a compound library list to NIST MSP format

Source: R/export_msp.R
export_msp.Rd

Writes a named list of compounds (as returned by import_msp) to a NIST-standard .msp file. Each compound is written as a self-contained block with metadata fields followed by its peak list.

Use this function for:

  • Saving a filtered or deduplicated library back to disk

  • Exporting processed libraries for use in other tools (e.g. NIST MS Search, MZmine, MS-DIAL)

  • Archiving subsets produced by import_msp

Usage

export_msp(
  library,
  file_path = "library_export.msp",
  fields = c("Name", "PrecursorMZ", "Adduct", "Formula", "ExactMass", "InChIKey",
    "InChI", "SMILES", "IonMode", "CollisionEnergy", "InstrumentType", "Instrument",
    "IonizationType", "Spectrum_type", "Comments"),
  mz_digits = 4L,
  intensity_digits = 0L
)

Arguments

library

A named list of compounds as returned by import_msp. Each element must contain a Peaks data frame with columns mz and rel_intensity, plus any metadata fields to be written.

file_path

Path to the output .msp file. Parent directory must exist. Existing files are overwritten.

fields

Character vector of metadata field names to write for each compound, in the order they will appear in the output. Fields absent from a compound are silently skipped. Defaults to all standard NIST MSP fields: c("Name", "PrecursorMZ", "Adduct", "Formula", "ExactMass", "InChIKey", "InChI", "SMILES", "IonMode", "CollisionEnergy", "InstrumentType", "Instrument", "IonizationType", "Spectrum_type", "Comments").

mz_digits

Integer. Number of decimal places for mz values in the peak list. Default 4.

intensity_digits

Integer. Number of decimal places for intensity values in the peak list. Default 0 (integer-like output, consistent with NIST convention).

Value

Invisibly returns file_path. Called primarily for its side effect of writing the .msp file.

See also

import_msp, convert_to_nist_msp

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Round-trip: import, filter, export
CBIO_library <- import_msp(
  system.file("extdata", "CBIO", "CBIO_Standards.msp", package = "MS1Match"),
  ionPolarity   = "pos",
  spectrum_type = "MS1",
  filter        = list(field = "Comments", pattern = "MSMLS")
)

export_msp(
  library   = CBIO_library,
  file_path = "CBIO_MSMLS_filtered.msp"
)

# Custom field order and precision
export_msp(
  library          = CBIO_library,
  file_path        = "CBIO_MSMLS_filtered.msp",
  fields           = c("Name", "Formula", "ExactMass", "Adduct",
                       "IonMode", "Comments"),
  mz_digits        = 6,
  intensity_digits = 2
)
} # }
